subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Why Intake Design Matters
description: A short lesson to help you apply Why Intake Design Matters.

hook.text: An engine is essentially an air pump—the more air it breathes, the more power it makes.

buildup.text: Intake runners, plenums, and throttle bodies are carefully shaped to guide air smoothly.

discovery.text: Tuned intake lengths use pressure waves to ram extra air into cylinders at specific speeds.

twist.text: Variable manifolds change runner length on the fly, giving torque at low speed and power up top.

climax.text: BMW's DISA and Honda's dual-runner systems squeezed gains once requiring forced induction.

punchline.text: Shaping the air path is as important as the fuel itself.

quiz.question: How do tuned intake runners add power?
